result:
I found no new confirmed, reachable defect in this follow-up. Both evidence/test corrections are present in the final files and close the two gaps the first review raised. I only read files. I did not run the tests, tsc or the C oracle, and I did not recompute any SHA-256 or Git hash. Pass/fail results below come from the provided logs.

## 1. The six historical constructors
- **The fixture is wired correctly.** `fixtures/mystery-gift-legacy-v2.json` has six entries. The first entry's blob `7365d527` matches the pre-patch `data.ts` index in `final-staged.diff`, so the chain ends at the immediate base. The snippets cover three shapes: with `trainerId` and `gameStats`, with `gameStats` only, and with neither. All of them have `version:2`, `gender`, `boxes:[]` and `options`.
- **The test actually runs each snippet** (`mystery-gifts.test.ts:39-45`). It checks the snippet hash, strips the type syntax, runs the constructor for both genders, and confirms no `mysteryGifts` key exists before migration. After `ensureMysteryGiftSave` it checks the queue is empty and everything else equals the earlier `structuredClone` exactly. `followup-regressions.log:317` shows `ok 51`.
- **The load path can't produce other shapes.** `main.ts:60` `readSave` loads only from `localStorage` and only accepts `version===2`; there's no v1 upgrade path. I found no non-test code that deletes or reassigns `boxes`, `options` or `gender` on a saved State. The only hit is `tutorial.ts:4`, which works on a throwaway clone.
- **This closes initial limitation 2.** The helper comment now names both `heartgold-3d-v2` and `-qa` (`mystery-gifts.ts:19`).
- **Remaining gaps:**
  - That these are *all* reachable revisions rests on `additional-data-history.json` and the fixture metadata. I can't walk Git read-only.
  - The fixture proves what the constructors produced. It doesn't prove what older runtime code later wrote into those saves, although I found no current code that removes the required fields.

## 2. Cleanup assertion before the next root reset
- **The new checks run at the right moment** (`mystery-gifts.test.ts:91-92`). Right after the failed (`UnportedFixture`) run and the cancelled run, they read the private `mysteryGiftSession.save` and expect `null`, before any new root run. A new root run replaces the session object at `script.ts:118`, so checking first is what lets the test catch a missing `finish` clear.
- **The runtime makes that check meaningful.** Both paths reach `finish` (`script.ts:393` finally; `:120` for standard scripts), and `finish` clears the pointer only for the root run (`:116`). Child VMs share the same session object (`:99`).
- **The negative control fails where it should.** `cleanup-negative-control.log:5,12` is `not ok 1` with the message "failed run releases its pointer before any new root run" (`# fail 1`, `:11558`). The positive run passes, with 129/129 in the log.
- **Caveats on the control:**
  - The log doesn't show the mutant's diff (it ran a copy, `.mg-mutant-test.ts`). That only the clearing statement was removed is your claim, not something the log shows.
  - The test stops at the first failed assertion, so the cancel-path check never ran under the mutant. By reading the code, the same finally block would also fail it.
- **This closes initial limitation 5.**

## 3. Other follow-up items
- **The 16-Mart test now checks `VAR_MYSTERY_GIFT_CHECK`** against `Number(!!tag)` (`test:66`). That matches native `scr_seq_0144.s:26,50`.
- **The Mother fixture comment is corrected.**
- **Runtime unchanged:** `runtime-comment-equivalence.json` reports `"equivalent": true`. ScriptVM logic in the final diff matches what the first review saw.

## Limitations that still apply
- The C oracle uses an opaque `raw[256]` / u32-aligned payload union, not the real SDK payload.
- Tags 1..15 are initialized and queried only. Tag-specific checks, grants, messages and receiving (selectors 3–6) throw an explicit Unsupported and never consume queued bytes.
- `NopVar490` matches native but now lets other scripts run (`0002`, `0164`, and maps 117/232/307/315/317/403/471/490/492/504/522) without full-gameplay coverage.
- A malformed store that is present blocks every Mart entry, by design, and has no tested recovery or user-facing path.
- The Mart fixtures queue one slot/tag (slot 7, tag 3). The C160 native cases cover each slot and tag, and there is one TypeScript multi-slot ordering case. None of this claims full SDK receiving parity.
- Absent-store migration applies only to known local browser-v2 State, not `.sav` or foreign JSON import.
- Outer recovery in source/main/World (Mart OnTransition under `SourceActionRecovery` and actor refresh) is owned by the parent and not reviewed here.

This doesn't extend approval to main, UI, World, external gift receiving, or any future root integration.
